title: introduce-tenant-watchdog-and-soft-eviction-to-arrest-queue-sinks
creator: Miguel Torres
description: Customer escalations revealed recurring queue starvation and long-context tail latency across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Investigation points to an interaction between the continuous batcher prefetch handshake, admission reservoir accounting, and eviction hysteresis in the KV cache that causes tenant-level queue spirals. This ticket implements a low-risk mitigation (tenant watchdog + soft eviction policy + timebound prefetch throttle) and hardens telemetry and tests so we can confidently roll a runtime patch to runtime-1.19.
root_cause_summary: A race in the continuous-batcher prefetch handshake lets inflight reservations leak when long-context requests trigger eviction hysteresis. Leaked admission tokens allow long requests to monopolize admission windows and cause repeated KV eviction + repopulation cycles. The result is tenant-level queue amplification and small-request starvation under mixed-length waves.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy runtime-1.18 with continuous-batcher enabled and KV eviction hysteresis configured (default policy)
Create two tenant workloads: Tenant A with 90% small chat requests, Tenant B with intermittent long-context (> 8k tokens) summarize requests
Drive a microburst: 200 small requests/sec for Tenant A and 2 long-context requests/sec for Tenant B over 60s
Observe: per-host admission shows inflight reservation skew to Tenant B; small-request latency increases and p95/p99 tail for Tenant A spikes, KV eviction rate increases on hosts serving Tenant B
mitigation_actions: Add tenant_watchdog service that monitors per-tenant admission_balance and triggers soft-eviction or borrow-back when a tenant exceeds timebound reservation thresholds
Implement soft_eviction: mark cache entries as soft-evictable and avoid full immediate eviction if eviction rate > threshold; favors small-flow hot entries
Add prefetch_timebound: limit prefetch handshake to X ms (config default 500 -> clamp 200-1000) to avoid long-context stabilizing admissions during handshake races
Ship additional telemetry (tenant_queue_depth_{p50,p95,p99}, kv_eviction_rate, admission_leak_events) and an alert rule for sustained tenant imbalance
Create deterministic integration test that replicates mixed-length wave and validates that small-request p95 stays within SLO
rollout_plan: 2) Canary on Hosted (region us-west-2) for 2 hours with synthetic mixed-length load and on-call monitoring
3) Expand canary to 10% of Hosted for 12 hours; monitor tenant_queue_depth and kv_eviction_rate
4) For Dedicated: offer immediate patch to high-usage customers via reserved capacity rolling upgrade; coordinate with Solutions for maintenance windows
5) For Private: release tarball + upgrade guide; include a config snippet to enable tenant_watchdog and adjust prefetch_timebound; schedule 1:1 with customers that reported escalations
6) Post-rollout 48h soak and collect telemetry for a full incident postmortem
acceptance_criteria: Deployed runtime-1.19 with tenant_watchdog and soft_eviction in Hosted and no regression in basic throughput tests
Synthetic mixed-length workload shows p95 small-request latency reduced by >= 60% vs baseline under the same microburst pattern
No increase in request error rate or throughput regressions across dedicated pools in canaries
Telemetry exposes admission_leak_events and a dashboard and an alert created in Console
qa_notes: Use the provided repro harness: drive mixed-length workload (script in infra/tools/repro/mixed_wave.sh)
Verify both config permutations: soft_eviction=true/false and prefetch_timebound=200/500/1000; record latencies and eviction counters
Run private-upgrade smoke on an air-gapped image in staging environment; validate that existing customers' prefetch knobs are preserved
Coordinate with on-call (pager: infra-oncall) during canary windows
